answer: A small ripple of new accounts can swell into an ocean of fake identities, and this design stops that flood. Each agent must answer a random beacon challenge and keep a compute heartbeat proving live work; a missed heartbeat suspends voting weight until a fresh check passes. A public record of results lets peers verify any history. Making 100 fakes means 100 live challenges and 100 workloads, costing 100 times the compute, while one honest agent answers one check. Standing builds slowly, like an opal forming over time, so newcomers cannot buy influence overnight.
